defects.description: The backoff exponent uses `retry_index` instead of `retry_index - 1`, so the first retry waits base_delay*multiplier rather than base_delay, shifting the whole geometric sequence one step too high.
paraphrases: The exponent is not decremented before raising the multiplier, so the initial wait already includes one growth step instead of starting at the configured base.
Every scheduled backoff is computed one geometric term ahead, making the very first delay base_delay*multiplier and inflating each subsequent one.
Because the index is used raw as the power, the series skips its base term and all attempts sleep longer than the policy specifies.

defects.description: Equal jitter subtracts the random component from the half-delay instead of adding it, producing values in [0, delay/2] rather than the intended [delay/2, delay], so backoffs systematically under-wait.
paraphrases: The 'equal' strategy should sit at half the delay and vary upward, but the minus sign pulls its results into the lower half of the range.
Jittered equal backoffs collapse toward zero because the random slice is deducted from the fixed half rather than stacked on top of it.
Instead of a guaranteed half plus some extra, the value becomes a half minus some amount, so an equal-jittered wait never exceeds 50% of the computed delay.

defects.description: The deadline check direction is reversed (`<=` instead of `>=`), so a policy with a deadline aborts with a 'deadline' RetryError while budget still remains, and conversely fails to stop once the budget is genuinely exhausted.
paraphrases: The comparison against the time budget runs backwards, tripping the timeout on the first retry whenever elapsed time is still comfortably within the allotment.
A deadline-bounded call bails out as soon as it has spent less than its budget, because the guard fires while elapsed remains below the deadline rather than beyond it.
The short-circuit treats 'time still left' as 'time is up', so the retry loop raises the deadline error prematurely and only skips the check once truly over budget.

defects.description: When no retryable exception types are configured, should_retry_exception returns True instead of False, so a policy built with retry_on=None retries every exception rather than letting it propagate immediately.
paraphrases: An empty set of retryable exception classes is meant to mean 'retry nothing', yet the early-out reports retryable, causing all raised errors to be retried.
With no exception types registered the method wrongly classifies every exception as eligible for retry, contradicting the 'anything else propagates immediately' contract.
The no-configured-types branch yields the wrong boolean, effectively turning retry_on=None into retry-on-any-exception.

gray_zones.note: _normalize_exc_types performs tuple(exc) for any iterable without checking that its elements are exception classes, so a malformed retry_on (e.g. a list containing non-types) is accepted silently at construction and only fails later as a TypeError inside isinstance(). A defensible robustness concern, but not one of the injected defects.
